thread:
incident_bot: :rotating_light: Pager: elevated 5xx + auth errors in AWS eu-central-1 affecting Hosted API and Dedicated pools. Pager link: https://pager.redwood.internal/p/5968123456

mike_oncall: I'm on it, grabbing graphs.

anna_sre: seeing ~65% 5xx on /v1/generate from eu-central-1, median latency up to 700ms, some 502/504s. Dedicated pool nodes showing failed auth to STS when refreshing creds.

jess_prod: customer impact: some customers on Dedicated eu-central are hitting request failures; hosted customers routed to eu-central see higher latencies and occasional timeouts.

rodrigo_infra: AWS Health shows elevated throttling on IAM/STSSecureTokenService in eu-central-1: https://status.aws.amazon.com/incidents/xxxxx. Suspect token exchange failures causing our auth proxy to return 502 upstream.

mike_oncall: can we throttle retries and route traffic away from eu-central while AWS recovers?

rodrigo_infra: yes. Plan: 1) reduce retry multiplier in auth proxy 2) shift external-facing traffic -> eu-west-1 / ap-northeast-1 3) failover Dedicated pools to reserve capacity in eu-west-1.

alex_support: I'll open a customer-impact doc and notify SLT + affected customers (only those with eu-central tenancy).

sarah_eng: posting quick mitigation commands here, will execute once approved:
```bash
# reduce retry multiplier
kubectl -n infra set env deployment/auth-proxy RETRY_BACKOFF_MULT=0.5

# update global routing weights (edge config)
edgectl update-pool-weights --prefix /v1 --region eu-west-1=0.6 --region ap-northeast-1=0.25 --region eu-central-1=0.15
```

mike_oncall: go ahead, Rodrigo + Sarah followup to validate. I will assume pager duty until handoff.

rodrigo_infra: applied auth-proxy env change, reduced retries.

sarah_eng: pushed edge weight update, canary 10% for 2 minutes then full. Monitoring now.

incident_bot: Deploy notification: edge-config-bump by sarah_eng at 5968123789.

anna_sre: metrics: error-rate eu-central-1 dropping from 65% -> 20% over 3m after routing change. Latency median down to 240ms. Dedicated pool failovers showing successful reconnections to STS via eu-west-1.

jess_prod: Customer update draft: "We're experiencing elevated errors in eu-central-1 caused by third-party auth service degradation. We've routed traffic to healthy regions and reduced retries; impact is decreasing. We'll follow up after AWS confirms service recovery." Alex please send.

alex_support: sent to impacted customers + posted internal #customers-notify.

mike_oncall: quick handoff: I'm passing oncall to anna_sre for monitoring and postmortem. Anna, please keep incident ticket updated and file AWS support case for root cause correlation.

anna_sre: taking oncall. Opening AWS support case now (case# INC-2026-000123). Also will collect STS logs and auth-proxy traces for postmortem.

rodrigo_infra: next steps: increase token cache TTL to reduce STS calls (temp), validate long-term retry/backoff tuning, add regional circuit-breaker to avoid cascading failures when cloud provider throttles.

sarah_eng: noted. I'll add an eval to Redwood Optimize to surface STS/token call frequency per model route.

incident_bot: Incident status -> mitigated (partial) at 5968124095. Remaining: watch for full AWS recovery before reverting routing.

anna_sre: summary for incident log: cause: AWS STS/iam egress throttling in eu-central-1 causing auth failures and 5xx in hosted + dedicated; mitigation: reduced retry multiplier, edge weight shift to eu-west-1/ap-northeast-1, increased token caching, customer notifications; next steps: postmortem, AWS case, circuit-breaker + config defaults.

mike_oncall: thanks team. If AWS posts recovery, we'll plan gradual re-weighting and verify no regression. :thumbsup:
